title: Indian-American Sahith Theegala in Contention at The Open Championship at Royal Birkdale

body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sahith Theegala is tied for 30th at The Open Championship with an even-par score.
  • The tournament features a total purse of $17.75 million, one of golf's richest events.
  • The projected cut is around two or three over par, favoring Theegala's chances to advance.
  • Theegala and Akshay Bhatia highlight growing Indian-American representation in professional golf.
  • The Open Championship runs through July 19, with coverage on NBC and Peacock.

Indian-American golfer Sahith Theegala is firmly in contention at the 2026 Open Championship, sitting in a tie for 30th at even par through the first round at Royal Birkdale Golf Club in Southport, England. As the second round got underway on Friday, Theegala was looking to push up the leaderboard and secure his spot for the weekend rounds at golf's oldest major.

Solid Start at Royal Birkdale

Theegala carded an even-par 70 in Thursday's opening round, keeping himself well within the projected cut line at the storied English links course. He teed off for the second round at 1:57 a.m. ET on Friday, grouped with Michael Brennan and Laurie Canter in the early wave.

The tournament is headlined by Australian Lucas Herbert, who fired a spectacular eight-under-par 62 to seize the outright lead. Cameron Young and Jackson Suber share second place at six under, while Bryson DeChambeau, Ryan Gerard, and Sam Burns are tied for fourth at five under.

The Open Championship carries a total purse of $17.75 million this year, making it one of the richest events in golf history. The tournament returns to Royal Birkdale for the 11th time, with the venue last hosting the event in 2017 when Jordan Spieth claimed the Claret Jug.

Indian-American Representation on Golf's Biggest Stage

Theegala, born in Orange, California to Telugu immigrant parents from India, has become one of the most prominent golfers of Indian descent on the PGA Tour. The Pepperdine University alumnus has established himself as a consistent presence on the world's premier golf circuit and a fan favorite known for his aggressive style of play.

His appearance at Royal Birkdale is part of a growing trend of Indian-American representation at golf's highest level. Fellow Indian-American Akshay Bhatia is also competing at The Open, sitting at even par through his first round. The presence of two golfers of Indian heritage at the sport's most prestigious championship underscores the growing influence of the diaspora in a sport that has historically seen limited South Asian participation.

What's at Stake

The projected cut at Royal Birkdale is expected to fall around two or three over par, meaning Theegala's even-par score leaves him in a comfortable position to advance to the weekend rounds. A strong Friday showing could push him into the top 20 and contention for a significant payday.

For Indian Americans following the tournament from across the United States, Theegala's presence in the field is a source of community pride. As golf continues to globalize and diversify, players like Theegala and Bhatia are breaking barriers and inspiring a new generation of Indian-origin golfers to take up the sport.

The Open Championship continues through Sunday, July 19, with weekend coverage on NBC and streaming on Peacock.
